decisions.reason: By now the launch uncertainty should be clearer, but because particle-therapy QA is strategically important and differentiated, we would still retain the product unless demand has plainly disappointed.
As a low-cost chamber squarely in our core dosimetry range, it remains worth keeping after several years absent clear evidence of weak demand.
This chamber faces more portfolio-overlap risk than B, yet the carrying cost is likely modest and the option value of serving a distinct small-volume use case still justifies retention.
Its relative-dosimetry specialization complements the measurement portfolio and is likely inexpensive to maintain, so we would keep it while it supports a complete offering.
A thimble chamber is a standard item in clinic QA, and despite some overlap its role in a full chamber lineup still outweighs the benefit of withdrawing it now.
